??? quote "Dialogue"

    - Hm. Forty years I have kept this fire, and it has never once burned low. It will not start because a visitor stands too close. Well. Since you are here, sit.
    - That bark you brought burns slow and steady. The fire likes it. So do I, though I will not say so twice.
    - You carried my words to the Old One. Good. Some things a keeper cannot say in council. The fire hears them, and now Hask has too.
    - The fire is listening. So am I, more or less.
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* Tell me a Kragvar song.
        - *Choice:* How was the council?
        - *Choice:* Goodbye.
    - Ulm, keeper of the council fire. I was a mason once, with stone dust in my beard instead of ash. When the family looked to me for chieftain, I said no: the keeper does not leave the fire. My brother Baruk took it instead.
    - The songs say the best of the Kragvar did not come home from the war. They stayed beneath the World Tree to keep watch. My grandson Korrin sits on the woodpile and listens to every word.
    - Sometimes I wonder whether anyone down there still sings our names back. Nobody comes up the road to tell me. So I keep the fire, and I keep singing.
    - Loud, as always. Four families, four kinds of pride. The Old One sits with me late after, and we say to the fire what nobody said to each other.
    - Go on. The fire and I have things to talk over.
